id_and_class.theory_title: Schelling’s Nature, Spirit, and the Identity of Mind
id_and_class.summary: Schelling holds that mind and nature are two poles of one absolute reality: ‘nature is visible spirit, spirit is invisible nature’. Nature is a self-organizing productivity with an unconscious, proto-mental side that rises through graded stages until, in human beings, it awakens to self-consciousness. Consciousness is thus nature becoming aware of itself, and it always rests on an unconscious ground it cannot make fully transparent.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Nature Awakening to Itself

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is the self-manifestation of an originally unconscious, productive nature that divides itself into subject and object and becomes luminous to itself in finite self-consciousness.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Real and ideal are two views of one and the same substance. Mental and physical orders express a more basic identity, with neither reduced to the other.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Developmental emergence: self-consciousness is an achievement reached in stages, but it unfolds from a nature that is already inwardly proto-mental, not from inert matter.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: The subject develops through a ‘history of self-consciousness’ from sensation to productive intuition, reflection, and will. Reflection necessarily splits knower from known, so consciousness both discloses and loses the prior unity of subject and object.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Sensation is the first-person side of nature's self-differentiation, the point where nature's productive tensions are felt inwardly. How this yields determinate qualities remains metaphysical, not worked out in detail.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: One absolute reality; nature as living productivity that appears only in its products; polar oppositions (subject/object, real/ideal, conscious/unconscious); an unconscious ground of will and drive.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Speculative philosophy of nature and transcendental reflection. Art gives the fullest access, showing the identity of conscious and unconscious that discursive thought cannot state.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Nature's products are temporary stabilizations of deeper activity, like eddies in a stream. They form a graded series from inorganic nature through organisms and sensation to self-conscious human beings.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Sensation; self-consciousness; the unconscious; freedom and will; aesthetic experience.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Self-inhibiting productivity. Nature becomes determinate by limiting itself, producing polar tensions, and consciousness arises when those tensions become felt from within.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness is a dynamic, developmental process: nature ascends through stages until it awakens to itself in humans, and individual self-consciousness passes through stages from sensation to will.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Proto-mentality runs through all of nature; full self-consciousness appears in human beings.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness is nature's own coming-to-awareness. In the later freedom writings it is rooted in will, darkness, drive, and the possibility of evil.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Subject and object are differentiated within a prior unity, so unity comes first and division is secondary. Artistic production reunites conscious intention with unconscious productivity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Experience is not an inner copy of an outer world; the world becomes manifest through nature's self-differentiation into knower and known.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Nature is a graded, self-organizing process whose higher products include organism, sensation, and consciousness. Schelling's account is metaphysical, not Darwinian.
core_claims_and_evidence: Nature is visible spirit and spirit is invisible nature, two aspects of one reality.
Kant left unclear how a free, knowing subject arises within deterministic nature, which a productive, inwardly subjective nature explains.
Self-consciousness cannot fully ground itself because it depends on unconscious productivity, bodily nature, and drives.
Art displays the identity of freedom and nature that philosophy cannot fully state.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Metaphysical and transcendental argument, with art treated as a form of disclosure.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The account lacks operational detail: the passage from dynamic nature to determinate phenomenal qualities stays metaphysical. Schelling's system also changed repeatedly, from philosophy of nature to identity philosophy to the late philosophy of freedom.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Schelling does not specify how unconscious productivity becomes a felt, first-person point of view, or how the stages of nature map onto actual organisms.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a monism that avoids both materialism and subjective idealism. It anticipates dual-aspect monism, panpsychism, cosmopsychism, Bradley's absolute idealism, and psychoanalytic theories of the unconscious.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Consciousness is nature's own self-revelation, so human self-awareness completes a process built into reality itself.
